blocks.content: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 constitutionalised urban local government and added Part IX-A and the 12th Schedule to the Constitution of India.

rows: State Legislative Act (or Parliament Act for UTs)

items: Distinguish between the Mayor (political titular head elected by members/citizens) and the Municipal Commissioner (executive head usually from the IAS cadre).
Remember that the 12th Schedule has 18 functional items for Municipalities, whereas the 11th Schedule has 29 functional items for Panchayats.
Note the constitutional provisions: Article 243-ZD mandates a District Planning Committee, and Article 243-ZE mandates a Metropolitan Planning Committee.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 constitutionalised urban local bodies and added Part IX-A (Articles 243-P to 243-ZG) to the Constitution.
Urban local governance features a three-tier structure: Nagar Panchayat for transitional areas, Municipal Council for smaller urban areas, and Municipal Corporation for larger urban areas.
The Mayor is the formal political head and first citizen of the city, presiding over meetings of the Municipal Corporation.
The Municipal Commissioner serves as the chief executive officer responsible for implementing council decisions and is appointed by the State Government.
The 12th Schedule contains 18 functional matters devolved to urban local government institutions.
